children: Producer prices in Malta increased 1.5% year-on-year in July 2026, matching the reading of the previous two months and remaining at their highest level since October 2023.
Energy prices remained unchanged from the previous month.
Meanwhile, prices for intermediate goods rose at a slower pace (1.6% vs 2.7%), while growth accelerated for capital goods (5.5% vs 5.0%).

Consumer goods inflation also rose to 0.7% after being unchanged in the previous month, with durable consumer goods steady at 0.1% and non-durable consumer goods increasing 0.7% after stagnating last month.
By market, producer inflation for the domestic market edged up (1.1% vs 1.0%), while it edged down for the non-domestic market (1.9% vs 2.1%).
On a monthly basis, producer prices inched higher to 0.3% in July  from a 0.2% increase in June, marking the highest since February.

title: Malta Producer Inflation Steady for 3 Months
